q: 补全 CAP 定理三要素：
q_en: Fill in the three properties of the CAP theorem:
text: CAP：{{Consistency}}（一致性）、{{Availability}}（可用性）、{{Partition tolerance}}（分区容错），分布式系统三者最多同时满足{{两}}个。
why: CAP 说三者不可兼得、最多取二。理解它是系统设计里定非功能需求的起点。
why_en: CAP says a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    CAP["CAP"] --> C["Consistency"]
    CAP --> A["Availability"]
    CAP --> P["Partition tolerance"]

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统在一致性、可用性、分区容错三者中最多同时满足两个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有节点在同一时刻看到相同的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistency means all nodes see the same data at the same time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 未失败节点的每个请求都能得到响应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Availability means every request to a non-failing node gets a response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 即使节点间消息丢失或网络分区，系统仍继续运行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partition tolerance means the system keeps operating despite message loss or network partitions between nodes.

scenario: 订单服务跨 3 个可用区部署，产品要求下单后从任意节点读都必须看到这笔新状态。
scenario_en: An order service runs across three availability zones, and the product requires that right after a write, a read from any node already sees the new state.
q: CAP 里的「一致性（Consistency）」指的是？
q_en: What does "Consistency" mean in CAP theorem?
options: 未失败节点的每个请求都能拿到响应
该笔事务满足原子性等 ACID 四要素
网络分区发生时系统仍继续对外提供服务
所有节点同时看到同一份数据，写后立刻读到新值
options_en: Every request to a non-failing node gets a response.
The transaction satisfies ACID properties.
The system keeps running even during a network partition.
All nodes see the same data at once, so a read right after a write returns the new value.
why: CAP 的一致性 = 所有节点同时看到同一份数据，写入后任意节点的后续读都返回最新值。注意它和 ACID 的 C 含义不同。
why_en: CAP consistency means all nodes see the same data at once, so after a write any subsequent read returns the updated value.
optionExplanations: 这是可用性的定义，不是一致性。
ACID 的 C 和 CAP 的 C 含义完全不同。
这是分区容错的定义。
正确，这就是 CAP 一致性的核心——所有节点同步看到最新数据。
optionExplanations_en: This describes Availability, not Consistency.
ACID consistency is fundamentally different from CAP consistency.
This describes Partition Tolerance.
Correct, this defines CAP consistency - all nodes immediately see the latest data.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统在一致性、可用性、分区容错三者中最多同时满足两个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系数据库事务的四个经典保证：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID is the classic set of database transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

scenario: 全球边缘节点上的商品浏览服务，规定只要节点没宕机就必须给出响应，数据略旧可以接受。
scenario_en: A product-browsing service on global edge nodes must always answer as long as the node itself is up, and slightly stale data is acceptable.
q: CAP 里的「可用性（Availability）」指的是？
q_en: What does "Availability" mean in CAP theorem?
options: 所有节点在同一时刻看到完全一致的数据
系统组件永远不会宕机或失败
未失败节点的请求都有响应，但不保证是最新数据
每次写入都必须立刻持久化到磁盘
options_en: All nodes see fully identical data at the same instant.
The system components never crash or fail.
Every request to a non-failing node gets a response, but it is not guaranteed to be the latest data.
Every write must be durably persisted to disk immediately.
why: 可用性 = 对未失败节点的每个请求都有响应，但不保证内容是最新的。「有个（可能旧的）答复」优于「报错」。
why_en: Availability means every request to a non-failing node gets a response, without a guarantee it holds the most recent data.
optionExplanations: 这是一致性的定义，不是可用性。
「永不宕机」是理想，但可用性允许有失败节点。
正确，这是可用性的核心——有答复比没答复好，即使答复可能旧。
持久化和可用性关系不大。
optionExplanations_en: This describes Consistency, not Availability.
Never crashing is an ideal, but Availability allows failed nodes as long as others respond.
Correct, this is Availability - a stale answer is better than no answer at all.
Durability is a separate concern from Availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统在一致性、可用性、分区容错三者中最多同时满足两个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

scenario: 跨两个机房的消息系统，机房间专线偶发中断、消息丢失，业务要求此时系统仍继续运行。
scenario_en: A messaging system spans two data centers whose link drops packets from time to time, and the business needs it to keep running through that.
q: CAP 里的「分区容错（Partition Tolerance）」指的是？
q_en: What does "Partition Tolerance" mean in CAP theorem?
options: 所有节点的读都返回最新一次写入
把数据切分成多个分片分别存储
节点间消息丢失或网络分区时，系统仍继续运行
系统能够容忍磁盘硬件损坏故障
options_en: Every node's read returns the most recent write.
Data is split and stored across multiple shards.
The system keeps operating even when messages are lost or the network is partitioned between nodes.
The system can tolerate physical disk hardware failures.
why: 分区容错 = 即使节点间任意消息丢失或网络分区，系统仍继续工作。它和数据分片（sharding）不是一回事。
why_en: Partition tolerance means the system keeps operating despite arbitrary message loss or network partitions between nodes.
optionExplanations: 这是一致性的表述。
数据分片（sharding）是存储优化，与分区容错（partition tolerance）无关。
正确，分区容错就是系统能继续工作，即使网络故障导致节点间通信中断。
磁盘容错和网络分区容错是不同的概念。
optionExplanations_en: This describes Consistency.
Data sharding is a storage technique, completely unrelated to partition tolerance.
Correct, partition tolerance means continuing to operate despite network partitions between nodes.
Disk fault tolerance is different from network partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统在一致性、可用性、分区容错三者中最多同时满足两个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据切分成多个分片分别存储，用来扩展写入和存储容量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across multiple partitions to scale storage and writes.

scenario: 面试中要用 CAP 快速做决策，不想在「三选二」上纠结。
scenario_en: You need to use CAP to make a fast interview decision instead of getting stuck picking two out of three.
q: 实践中把 CAP 简化成一个选择的关键洞察是？
q_en: What is the key insight that reduces CAP to a single practical choice?
options: 牺牲分区容错，换取同时拥有一致性与可用性
分区容错必须保留，真正的取舍是分区时选一致性还是可用性
分布式系统能同时满足一致性可用性和分区容错
任何场景下一致性都优先于可用性
options_en: Give up partition tolerance to keep both consistency and availability.
Partition tolerance is mandatory, so the real choice is consistency or availability during a partition.
A distributed system can satisfy all three properties at once.
Consistency always outranks availability in every scenario.
why: 网络故障必然发生，所以 P 不可放弃。于是 CAP 实际归结为一个问题：分区发生时，你选 C 还是选 A？
why_en: Since network failures are inevitable, partition tolerance is mandatory, so CAP reduces to choosing consistency or availability when a partition occurs.
whenOtherWins: 只有在「绝不会分区」的单机系统里才谈得上同时拥有 C 和 A——但那就不是分布式系统了。
tradeoff: 一致性 vs 可用性（分区容错是前提，不是可选项）
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Distributed["Distributed system"] --> P["Partition tolerance required"]
    P --> Choice{"During partition"}
    Choice --> C["Choose C"]
    Choice --> A["Choose A"]
optionExplanations: 在分布式系统中，网络分区必然发生，P 不能放弃。
正确，这是 CAP 最实用的理解——P 必须有，真正的权衡在 C 和 A 之间。
现实分布式系统无法同时三要素，这与 CAP 定理矛盾。
C 和 A 的优先级取决于具体场景，不是绝对的。
optionExplanations_en: In distributed systems, network partitions inevitably occur, so P cannot be abandoned.
Correct, this is the practical takeaway - P is mandatory, so you really choose between C and A when a partition happens.
Distributed systems cannot achieve all three simultaneously, contradicting the CAP theorem.
Whether C or A is more important depends on the scenario, not absolute.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统在一致性、可用性、分区容错三者中最多同时满足两个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点间网络中断或消息丢失，导致部分节点无法互相通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A network partition is a break in connectivity between nodes so some cannot exchange messages.

scenario: 跨机房的银行转账服务，网络断开期间绝不能返回不确定是否最新的账户余额。
scenario_en: A bank transfer service spans data centers, and while the link is down it must never hand back a balance that might not be the latest.
q: 网络分区发生时，选择「一致性」意味着系统会怎么表现？
q_en: During a network partition, what does choosing "consistency" mean for system behavior?
options: 宁可暂时返回过期的旧数据，也要保持系统响应
分区期间系统会自动修复底层网络故障
无论是否分区都保证数据最新且系统永远可用
宁可报错拒绝请求，也不返回不确定是否最新的数据
options_en: Keep responding by serving data that may already be stale.
Automatically repair the underlying network failure.
Guarantee both freshness and availability regardless of partitions.
Reject the request with an error rather than return data that might not be the latest.
why: 分区时选一致性（CP）= 无法保证最新就宁可报错/不可用；选可用性（AP）= 照样响应，但可能给旧数据。这是同一枚硬币的两面。
why_en: Choosing consistency during a partition means returning an error rather than serving data that might be stale.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Partition["Network partition"] --> C["Prefer C"]
    C --> Reject["Reject uncertain request"]
    Reject --> Fresh["Never serve stale"]
optionExplanations: 这是选择可用性（AP）的表现，不是一致性。
系统无法自动修复网络故障。
网络分区时不可能同时拥有最新和可用，这是 CAP 的核心。
正确，选一致性（CP）意味着无法保证最新就宁可报错，保证不返回错误数据。
optionExplanations_en: This is what choosing Availability (AP) looks like, not Consistency.
Systems cannot auto-repair network failures.
During a partition, you cannot have both fresh data and availability - this is CAP's core.
Correct, choosing Consistency (CP) means rejecting uncertain requests rather than serving stale data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点间网络中断或消息丢失，导致部分节点无法互相通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A network partition is a break in connectivity between nodes so some cannot exchange messages.

scenario: 美国和欧洲各一台服务器，用户 A 改了公开昵称。此时两地网络分区，欧洲的用户 B 想看 A 的资料。
scenario_en: You run one server in the US and one in Europe. User A changes their public nickname, then a network partition splits the two regions while User B in Europe tries to view A's profile.
q: 这个场景更该选？
q_en: Which should this scenario prioritize?
options: 一致性：分区期间返回错误，不显示资料
可用性：显示可能过期的旧昵称
两者都要，阻塞直到网络恢复
直接下线服务
options_en: Consistency: return an error and show no profile during the partition.
Availability: show the possibly-stale old nickname.
Both: block the request until the network recovers.
Take the service offline entirely.
why: 看资料这种场景，显示旧昵称远好过报错。「看到旧名字」优于「什么都看不到」，所以选可用性、接受最终一致。
why_en: For viewing a profile, showing a slightly stale name beats showing an error, so prioritize availability.
whenOtherWins: 如果这份数据是订座、库存、余额这类「错了就出事」的，则必须反过来选一致性。
tradeoff: 可用性 vs 一致性：展示旧昵称 vs 报错拒绝服务
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Partition["Network partition"] --> A["Prefer A"]
    A --> Serve["Keep responding"]
    Serve --> Stale["May return stale data"]
    Stale --> Converge["Converge later"]
optionExplanations: 看资料时返回错误太糟糕，用户会很不满。
正确，看个资料显示旧昵称影响很小，可用性优先。
阻塞不现实，用户无法接受。
下线服务比显示旧数据更差。
optionExplanations_en: Returning an error when viewing a profile is terrible for user experience.
Correct, showing a slightly stale nickname for viewing a profile is acceptable, so prioritize availability.
Blocking until consistency is impractical and users won't accept it.
Taking the service offline is worse than showing slightly outdated data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点间网络中断或消息丢失，导致部分节点无法互相通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A network partition is a break in connectivity between nodes so some cannot exchange messages.

scenario: 航班选座：用户 A 订了 6A，但网络分区导致用户 B 那边仍显示 6A 可选，B 也订了同一个座位。
scenario_en: Flight seat booking: User A books seat 6A, but a network partition leaves User B's view showing 6A as still open, so B also books it.
q: 这类订票系统该优先？
q_en: What should this kind of booking system prioritize?
options: 优先可用性，允许两人都能选座下单
选哪个都无所谓，不影响结果
分区容错可以直接放弃不做
优先一致性，避免同一座位被重复预订
options_en: Prioritize availability so both users can pick a seat.
It doesn't matter which one you choose.
Partition tolerance can simply be dropped.
Prioritize consistency to avoid double-booking the same seat.
why: 重复预订同一座位是灾难性的，所以订票必须强一致：宁可分区时暂时不可下单，也不能超卖出双份座位。
why_en: Seat booking must prioritize consistency to prevent two people reserving the same seat during a partition.
whenOtherWins: 同一个订票系统里，「浏览活动详情」可以选可用性——展示略旧的介绍无伤大雅。
tradeoff: 一致性 vs 可用性：拒绝重复下单 vs 允许两人都能选座
optionExplanations: 在订票系统选可用性会导致超卖灾难。
这关系到业务，无所谓是错的。
P 无法放弃，P 是分布式系统必须的。
正确，重复预订同一座位是灾难，必须强一致。
optionExplanations_en: Choosing Availability in a booking system could lead to double-booking disasters.
This affects the business critically, so it definitely matters.
P cannot be dropped; P is mandatory for any distributed system.
Correct, double-booking the same seat is catastrophic, so Consistency is mandatory.

scenario: 电商只剩最后一支牙刷，网络分区期间系统对多个用户都显示「有货」。
scenario_en: An e-commerce site has exactly one toothbrush left in stock, and during a network partition it shows "in stock" to multiple users at once.
q: 为避免超卖，应优先？
q_en: To avoid overselling, what should be prioritized?
options: 优先可用性，允许显示有货
用最终一致即可，短暂超卖没关系
优先一致性，库存扣减不能超卖
随机选一个方向就行
options_en: Prioritize availability and keep showing it as in stock.
Eventual consistency is fine even with brief overselling.
Prioritize consistency so inventory can never be oversold.
Just pick a direction at random.
why: 库存扣减必须强一致，否则会把仅剩的 1 件卖给多个用户造成超卖。分区时宁可暂时不可售，也不能超卖。
why_en: E-commerce inventory needs consistency so the last item is not oversold to multiple users during a partition.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是展示「大概还有货」的粗略状态，可以选可用性；但真正的下单扣减这一步必须强一致。
tradeoff: 一致性 vs 可用性：拒绝超卖 vs 保持显示可购买
optionExplanations: 优先可用性会导致最后一件卖给多个用户。
最终一致无法防止超卖灾难。
正确，库存这类关键数据必须强一致。
随机选择是不负责的。
optionExplanations_en: Prioritizing Availability would result in selling the last item to multiple users.
Eventual consistency cannot prevent the overselling disaster.
Correct, critical data like inventory needs strong consistency.
Randomly choosing is irresponsible and breaks the system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在一段时间后趋于一致，但短期内可能不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means the system converges to a consistent state over time but may be briefly inconsistent.

scenario: 股票交易平台展示订单簿（order book），价格瞬息万变。
scenario_en: A stock-trading platform displays the order book, where prices change second by second.
q: 该优先？
q_en: What should this platform prioritize?
options: 优先一致性：订单簿必须准确最新，避免按错误价格成交
优先可用性：展示旧价格延迟一点也没关系
一致性和可用性两者都不重要
只需要保证分区容错就足够了
options_en: Prioritize consistency: the order book must be accurate and current, to avoid trading at wrong prices.
Prioritize availability: showing a slightly stale price is fine.
Neither consistency nor availability matters here.
Only partition tolerance needs to be guaranteed.
why: 金融/交易系统展示旧价格可能导致按错误价格成交，属于灾难性后果，必须强一致。
why_en: Trading platforms need consistency because stale order-book data could cause trades at incorrect prices.
whenOtherWins: 行情的历史图表、公司简介这类周边信息可以选可用性；核心的实时订单簿不行。
tradeoff: 一致性 vs 可用性：订单簿必须精确 vs 允许旧价格
optionExplanations: 正确，金融交易按错误价格成交是灾难，必须强一致。
显示旧价格可能导致错误成交，在金融领域致命。
对交易平台来说很重要。
仅有 P 不够，还需 C 来保证交易正确。
optionExplanations_en: Correct, trading at wrong prices is catastrophic in finance, so Consistency is mandatory.
Showing stale prices could lead to trades at wrong prices, which is fatal.
This matters very much for a trading platform.
Having only P is not enough, C is also required to ensure correct trades.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录当前所有买卖报价和数量的实时列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An order book is the live list of current buy and sell price levels and quantities.

scenario: Netflix 有人更新了某部电影的简介文案，分区期间部分用户看到旧简介。
scenario_en: Netflix updates a movie's description; during a network partition some users still see the old text.
q: 内容平台这类场景该优先？
q_en: What should a content platform prioritize in this kind of scenario?
options: 优先一致性，宁可完全不显示简介
优先可用性，短暂显示旧简介完全可接受
直接放弃分区容错这一属性
阻塞请求直到数据完全一致为止
options_en: Prioritize consistency and show no description at all.
Prioritize availability; briefly showing the old description is fine.
Simply drop partition tolerance.
Block the request until data is fully consistent.
why: 内容平台展示略旧的简介不是灾难，可用性优先、接受最终一致——让用户始终能看到（哪怕稍旧的）内容。
why_en: Content platforms can prioritize availability because briefly showing an outdated description is not catastrophic.
whenOtherWins: 如果是支付、订阅扣费这类涉及钱的功能，同一个 Netflix 也要对那部分选一致性。
tradeoff: 可用性 vs 一致性：短暂旧简介 vs 完全不显示
optionExplanations: 不显示简介的用户体验太差。
正确，内容平台显示旧简介不是灾难，可用性优先。
P 无法放弃。
阻塞会导致糟糕的用户体验。
optionExplanations_en: Not showing a description gives poor user experience.
Correct, showing a slightly stale description on a content platform is not catastrophic, so prioritize Availability.
P cannot be abandoned.
Blocking for consistency would result in poor user experience.

scenario: 电商+社交混合平台逐功能定一致性级别，强一致成本高，只能给「错了就出事」的功能用。
scenario_en: On a platform mixing commerce and social features you set consistency per feature, and strong consistency is expensive enough to reserve for features where being wrong causes real damage.
q: 以下哪些场景「短暂不一致会是灾难」，因此应优先一致性？（多选）
q_en: In which of these scenarios would brief inconsistency be catastrophic, so consistency should be prioritized? (multi-select)
options: 航班/演出选座预订
电商最后一件库存的扣减
银行账户余额
社交媒体的头像更新
options_en: Flight or event seat booking.
Decrementing the last unit of e-commerce inventory.
Bank account balances.
Updating a social media profile avatar.
why: 订座、库存扣减、账户余额错了都会造成重复占用/超卖/丢钱，属灾难性，必须强一致；头像晚几分钟更新无所谓，可用性优先。
why_en: Seat booking, inventory decrement, and account balances need consistency, while a social avatar update can tolerate staleness.
tradeoff: 灾难级不一致（需一致性） vs 可容忍的短暂不一致（可用可用性）
optionExplanations: 正确，重复预订座位是灾难。
正确，超卖最后一件是灾难。
正确，账户余额错误会丢钱。
错误，头像晚更新无伤大雅，可以接受短暂不一致。
optionExplanations_en: Correct, double-booking seats is catastrophic.
Correct, overselling the last item is catastrophic.
Correct, account balance errors cause financial loss.
Wrong, avatar updates can tolerate delay and brief inconsistency.

scenario: 你在快速判断某个功能该选 C 还是 A。
scenario_en: You need to quickly decide whether a feature should favor consistency or availability.
q: 最该问自己的判定问题是？
q_en: What is the single question you should ask yourself?
options: 哪种技术方案实现起来相对更简单快捷？
团队现有数据库默认支持的是哪一种？
哪种方案带来的基础设施花费成本更低？
不一致算不算灾难？算就选一致性，不算就选可用性
options_en: Which technical approach is simpler and faster to implement?
Which one does the team's existing database support by default?
Which approach has lower infrastructure cost?
Would inconsistency be catastrophic? If yes pick consistency, if no pick availability.
why: 一句话判定：短暂不一致会不会造成灾难？会→一致性；不会→可用性。等价问法：「每次读都必须读到最新写吗？」
why_en: Ask whether briefly showing inconsistent data would be catastrophic: if yes choose consistency, if no choose availability.
whenOtherWins: 同一系统不同功能答案可以不同——所以要逐个功能问这个问题，而不是全局一刀切。
tradeoff: 一致性 vs 可用性：按「短暂不一致是否灾难」逐功能判定
optionExplanations: 实现的难度和业务需求无关，不是判定标准。
数据库选型应该跟着需求，而不是反过来。
成本考虑应该在业务需求之后。
正确，这是唯一该问的问题——错了会出事吗？
optionExplanations_en: Implementation difficulty is unrelated to business requirements and is not the decision criterion.
Database choice should follow requirements, not the other way around.
Cost considerations should follow business requirements, not drive them.
Correct, this is the only question that matters - will incorrect data cause problems?

scenario: 跨区数据库集群刚发生网络分区，值班工程师要预判两种选型此刻分别怎么回应客户端。
scenario_en: A cross-region database cluster just hit a network partition, and the on-call engineer needs to predict how each choice answers clients right now.
q: 在「分区期间如何响应」上，CP 系统与 AP 系统的区别是？
q_en: How do CP systems and AP systems differ in how they respond during a partition?
options: CP 系统返回旧数据，AP 系统直接报错拒绝
CP 宁可报错拒绝保正确；AP 照常响应可能给旧值
分区期间两者行为完全相同，都会报错
AP 系统遇到分区就直接停止服务
options_en: CP returns stale data while AP returns an error.
CP rejects rather than return stale data; AP keeps responding but may return stale data.
Both behave identically during a partition, both error out.
AP simply stops serving during a partition.
why: 分区时 CP 牺牲可用性保正确（报错/拒写），AP 牺牲一致性保响应（给旧值）。这是 CAP 权衡最实际的体现。
why_en: During a partition, a CP system errors rather than serve stale data, while an AP system stays responsive but may return stale data.
tradeoff: CP（拒绝保正确） vs AP（响应可能给旧值）
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Normal["No partition"] --> PACELC["PACELC"]
    PACELC --> L["Lower latency"]
    PACELC --> C["Stronger consistency"]
optionExplanations: 搞反了，CP 是拒绝，AP 是返回旧值。
正确，这是 C 和 A 最根本的差异。
行为完全不同。
AP 会继续响应，它不会停止服务。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed, CP rejects while AP returns stale data.
Correct, this is the fundamental difference between CP and AP systems.
Their behaviors are completely different.
AP continues responding, it doesn't stop service.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区时选择一致性、牺牲可用性的系统类别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CP system chooses consistency over availability when a partition occurs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区时选择可用性、牺牲强一致的系统类别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AP system chooses availability over strict consistency when a partition occurs.

scenario: 系统设计面试刚对齐完功能需求，进入非功能需求阶段。
scenario_en: You've just finished aligning on functional requirements in a system design interview and are moving into non-functional requirements.
q: 关于 CAP 该在何时讨论？
q_en: When should CAP be discussed?
options: 非功能需求阶段最先讨论：优先一致性还是可用性
等到把所有 API 接口都写完之后再讨论
只有被面试官主动问到才提一句
等画完所有数据库表结构之后再讨论
options_en: Discuss it first in the non-functional requirements phase: consistency or availability?
Wait until every API endpoint is fully written.
Only mention it if the interviewer explicitly asks.
Wait until the database schema is fully drawn.
why: CAP 应是非功能需求阶段的起点，因为它会深刻影响后续选型和架构。开场就问：「这个系统优先一致性还是可用性？」
why_en: Discuss CAP first in the non-functional requirements phase, since the consistency-versus-availability choice shapes the whole design.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统显然是单机/低规模、不涉及分布式复制，CAP 的分区权衡就没那么关键，可轻描淡写带过。
tradeoff: 尽早定调 CAP vs 拖到写完 API/表结构才讨论
optionExplanations: 正确，CAP 决策会影响整个架构选型，应最先讨论。
API 设计应该跟着 CAP 决策走，不是反过来。
不主动提才是风险。
数据库表设计应该跟着 CAP 决策。
optionExplanations_en: Correct, the CAP decision shapes the entire architecture, so discuss it first in non-functional requirements.
API design should follow the CAP decision, not the reverse.
Failing to bring it up proactively is riskier.
Database schema should be designed following the CAP decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统在一致性、可用性、分区容错三者中最多同时满足两个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统的质量属性要求，如一致性、可用性、延迟、扩展性，而非具体功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements are quality attributes like consistency, availability, latency, and scalability, as opposed to specific features.

scenario: 票务系统的座位锁定功能，超卖零容忍：宁可下单失败，也不能把同一座位卖出两次。
scenario_en: In a ticketing system's seat-locking feature, overselling is unacceptable: better to fail the booking than sell the same seat twice.
q: 若一个功能要「优先一致性」，下列哪些设计/技术是合适的方向？（多选）
q_en: If a feature must prioritize consistency, which of these designs/technologies fit? (multi-select)
options: 用两阶段提交（2PC）等分布式事务让多存储保持同步
用单节点方案，单一真相来源，避免传播不一致
传统 RDBMS（PostgreSQL/MySQL）、Google Spanner、DynamoDB 强一致模式
大量异步只读副本，读可落后于主库
options_en: Use distributed transactions like two-phase commit (2PC) to keep multiple stores in sync.
Use a single-node design with one source of truth to avoid propagation issues.
Use strongly-consistent stores: traditional RDBMS (PostgreSQL/MySQL), Google Spanner, or DynamoDB in strong mode.
Use lots of asynchronous read replicas where reads can lag the primary.
why: 优先一致性 → 分布式事务(2PC)、单节点单一真相、或强一致存储(RDBMS/Spanner/DynamoDB 强一致)。异步只读副本恰恰是为可用性、会带来陈旧，方向相反。
why_en: Prioritizing consistency points to distributed transactions, single-node designs, or strongly-consistent stores like RDBMS, Spanner, or DynamoDB in strong mode.
tradeoff: 强一致技术方向 vs 异步复制换可用性的方向
optionExplanations: 2PC 让多个存储互相确认才提交，挡住的是「一个库写成功、另一个没写成功」的不一致，代价是协调延迟变高。
把写集中到一个节点当唯一真相源，天然没有多副本同步问题，代价是这个节点会成为扩展瓶颈。
直接选原生强一致的存储，省掉自建一致性协议的成本，开箱就有「读到最新写」的保证。
异步副本读到的是稍旧的值，这条路服务的是可用性/读扩展，挡不住这里要的强一致要求。
optionExplanations_en: 2PC has every store confirm before committing, which blocks one store succeeding while another silently fails, at the cost of higher coordination latency.
Routing writes through one node as the single source of truth avoids multi-replica sync issues, but that node becomes the scaling bottleneck.
Picking a natively strong-consistency store skips building your own consistency protocol and gives you 'read reflects the latest write' out of the box.
Async replicas can lag behind the primary, so this path serves availability and read scaling, not the strong-consistency requirement here.
codeSample:
PREPARE tx501 -> cache: OK
PREPARE tx501 -> db:    OK
# both replied OK, safe to commit
COMMIT  tx501 -> cache, db
# if either had replied NO:
# ABORT tx501 -> rollback both stores

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式事务协议：先让所有参与者准备提交，全部同意后才真正提交，否则整体回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit is a distributed transaction protocol where all participants first prepare, and the transaction only commits if everyone agrees, otherwise it rolls back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传统关系型数据库管理系统，如 PostgreSQL、MySQL。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RDBMS stands for relational database management system, such as PostgreSQL or MySQL.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 的全球分布式强一致数据库，用 TrueTime 时钟做跨区同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Spanner is Google's globally distributed, strongly consistent database that uses the TrueTime clock for cross-region synchronization.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管 NoSQL 数据库，可配置强一致读或最终一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed NoSQL database that can be configured for strongly consistent or eventually consistent reads.

scenario: 新闻 App 的信息流读路径，峰值百万 QPS，晚几秒看到新帖可以，但不能给用户报错。
scenario_en: The feed read path of a news app peaks at a million QPS; seeing a post a few seconds late is fine, but returning an error to the user is not.
q: 若一个功能要「优先可用性」，下列哪些设计/技术是合适的方向？（多选）
q_en: If a feature must prioritize availability, which of these designs/technologies fit? (multi-select)
options: 多副本 + 异步复制，任何副本都能服务读（可能略旧）
用 CDC（变更数据捕获）把主库变更异步传播到副本/缓存
面向可用性的多副本/多 AZ 存储（如 Cassandra；DynamoDB/Redis 需说明一致性设置和故障语义）
对每次写做跨存储两阶段提交
options_en: Multiple replicas with async replication; any replica can serve reads (possibly slightly stale).
Use CDC (change data capture) to propagate primary changes to replicas/caches asynchronously.
Availability-oriented multi-replica/multi-AZ stores (e.g. Cassandra; DynamoDB/Redis need explicit consistency settings).
Run a cross-store two-phase commit on every write.
why: 优先可用性就选异步多副本、CDC 异步传播、AP 导向存储：Cassandra 典型，DynamoDB/Redis 需按配置确认范围。两阶段提交方向相反，是强一致机制。
why_en: Prioritizing availability points to async replicas, CDC propagation, and AP-oriented stores like Cassandra, while two-phase commit goes the opposite direction toward strong consistency.
tradeoff: 可用性导向的技术方向 vs 强一致导向的技术方向
optionExplanations: 多副本异步复制让任意副本都能就近响应读请求，挡住的是单点故障拖垮整体可用性，代价是副本可能读到稍旧的值。
CDC 把主库变更异步广播给下游，减掉的是下游系统等主库同步写入的阻塞压力，换来的是短暂的数据延迟。
Cassandra 这种为可用性设计的存储天生就有多副本容错；换成 DynamoDB 或 Redis 走这条路时，要先看清各自的一致性开关。
跨存储两阶段提交要求各方先互相确认才提交，反而增加了阻塞和不可用窗口，方向和可用性优先正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Async multi-replica replication lets any replica serve reads nearby, which blocks a single point of failure from taking the whole system down, at the cost of replicas sometimes lagging.
CDC asynchronously broadcasts primary changes downstream, taking the wait-on-primary-write pressure off downstream systems in exchange for brief data lag.
Cassandra, built for availability, ships multi-replica fault tolerance natively; picking DynamoDB or Redis for this instead means checking each one's own consistency switch first.
Cross-store two-phase commit makes every party wait for mutual confirmation before committing, which adds blocking and unavailability — the opposite of prioritizing availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获数据库变更并异步传播给下游副本、缓存或其他系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CDC captures database changes and streams them asynchronously to downstream replicas, caches, or other systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向可用性设计的分布式 NoSQL 数据库，默认可调一致性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a distributed NoSQL database designed for availability, with tunable consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存数据库，Redis Cluster 模式下副本间是异步复制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory data store; in Redis Cluster mode, replicas are updated asynchronously.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云厂商机房内独立的故障隔离单元，多 AZ 部署可提升可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Availability Zone is an isolated failure domain within a cloud region; deploying across multiple AZs improves availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式事务协议：先让所有参与者准备提交，全部同意后才真正提交，否则整体回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit is a distributed transaction protocol where all participants first prepare, and the transaction only commits if everyone agrees, otherwise it rolls back.

scenario: 同一个电商平台里既有支付扣款也有商品浏览，架构师要决定 CAP 策略该怎么落。
scenario_en: One e-commerce platform contains both payment debits and product browsing, and the architect has to decide how the CAP choice actually lands.
q: 关于真实大型系统如何应对 CAP，最准确的是？
q_en: What is the most accurate description of how real large-scale systems handle CAP?
options: 整个系统只能全局选一种：要么 CP 要么 AP
所有功能都应最终一致
所有功能都必须强一致
常常按功能混合：不同功能各自选 C 或 A
options_en: The whole system must pick one globally: either CP or AP.
Every feature should be eventually consistent.
Every feature must be strongly consistent.
Real systems often mix per feature: each feature picks C or A on its own.
why: 现实系统常按功能混合 C/A：同一个系统里，关键写路径强一致、浏览类读路径高可用。逐功能选，而非全局一刀切。
why_en: Real systems often mix consistency and availability per feature rather than choosing one globally.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    App["One product"] --> Critical["Critical path: strong"]
    App --> Display["Display path: eventual"]
    Critical --> Money["money / inventory"]
    Display --> Feed["feed / comments"]
optionExplanations: 错误，现实系统按功能混合，不是全局一刀切。
全最终一致会让订票、付款等关键功能失败。
全强一致太重，不现实。
正确，同一系统内不同功能有不同需求。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong, real systems mix per feature, not one global choice for the whole system.
All eventual consistency breaks critical functions like booking and payment.
All strong consistency is too expensive and impractical.
Correct, different features within the same system have different consistency needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统在一致性、可用性、分区容错三者中最多同时满足两个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

scenario: Ticketmaster：既有「订座」又有「浏览活动详情」两类功能。
scenario_en: Ticketmaster has both a seat-booking feature and an event-details browsing feature.
q: 更合理的 CAP 划分是？
q_en: What is the more sensible CAP split here?
options: 两者都用强一致，接受更高延迟
订座用一致性防重复预订，浏览详情用可用性接受略旧内容
两者都用可用性，接受短暂不一致
订座用可用性抢座更快，浏览详情反而用一致性
options_en: Use strong consistency everywhere and accept higher latency.
Use consistency for booking to prevent double-booking, and availability for browsing to accept slightly stale content.
Use availability everywhere and accept brief inconsistency.
Use availability for booking to grab seats faster, and consistency for browsing instead.
why: Ticketmaster 是按功能混合的经典例子：订座必须强一致防双订，浏览活动详情可高可用、接受略旧。
why_en: Ticketmaster uses strong consistency for booking to prevent double-booking but availability for browsing event details.
whenOtherWins: 如果是限量抢购的「浏览剩余票数」，为避免误导也可能要更强的一致——取决于错了会不会出事。
tradeoff: 订座：一致性 vs 浏览详情：可用性（同系统按功能拆分）
optionExplanations: 浏览活动详情不需要那么强的一致。
正确，这是 Ticketmaster 的实际做法。
订座必须强一致。
反了，订座是关键路径，浏览是非关键路径。
optionExplanations_en: Browsing event details does not need such strong consistency.
Correct, this is what Ticketmaster actually does in practice.
Booking must be strongly consistent to prevent double-booking.
Reversed, booking is critical path, browsing is non-critical path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线票务平台，涉及演出/体育赛事的选座与购票。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ticketmaster is an online ticketing platform for booking seats at events.

scenario: Tinder：既有「匹配」又有「浏览用户资料」两类功能。
scenario_en: Tinder has both a matching feature and a profile-browsing feature.
q: 更合理的 CAP 划分是？
q_en: What is the more sensible CAP split here?
options: 匹配一致性同时可见，浏览资料可用性接受略旧
两者都用可用性，接受匹配延迟出现
匹配用可用性，浏览资料反而用一致性
两者都用一致性，接受更高延迟
options_en: Use consistency for matching so both sides see it immediately, and availability for profile browsing to accept a slightly stale avatar.
Use availability everywhere and accept delayed matches.
Use availability for matching and consistency for profile browsing instead.
Use consistency everywhere and accept higher latency.
why: Tinder 也是按功能混合：匹配需一致（同时右滑要立即互相看到匹配），浏览资料可高可用（略旧头像无妨）。
why_en: Tinder uses consistency for matching so simultaneous right-swipes both see the match, but availability for viewing profiles.
tradeoff: 匹配：一致性 vs 浏览资料：可用性
optionExplanations: 正确，匹配是关键，资料浏览可以接受略旧头像。
同时右滑的匹配需要一致。
反了。
头像不需要那么强的一致。
optionExplanations_en: Correct, matching is critical and needs consistency, while profile browsing can tolerate slightly stale avatars.
Simultaneous right-swipes need consistency to see matches immediately.
Reversed, the other way around.
Avatar updates do not need such strong consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于地理位置的社交/约会应用，核心功能是双方互相右滑匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tinder is a location-based dating app where mutual right-swipes create a match.

q: 补全一致性强度谱（由强到弱）：
q_en: Complete the consistency spectrum from strongest to weakest:
text: {{强一致}}（所有读反映最新写）→ {{因果一致}}（相关事件顺序一致）→ {{读己之写}}（自己的更新立即可见）→ {{最终一致}}（一段时间后趋于一致）。
why: 一致性不是二元，而是一条谱。理解它能让你做更细的决策，而不是只在「强/最终」两极之间跳。
why_en: Consistency is a spectrum from strong to causal to read-your-own-writes to eventual.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有读都反映最近一次写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means every read reflects the most recent write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有依赖关系的事件对所有人呈现相同顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Causal consistency ensures dependent events appear in the same order to everyone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户总能立即看到自己的更新，别人可能稍晚才看到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-your-own-writes guarantees a user immediately sees their own updates, while others may see them later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统会随时间趋于一致，但短期内可能不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means the system converges over time but may be briefly inconsistent.

scenario: 银行账户余额，任何读都必须反映最近一次写。
scenario_en: A bank account balance must have every read reflect the most recent write.
q: 需要哪种一致性级别？
q_en: Which consistency level is required?
options: 最终一致，允许长时间才收敛
读己之写，仅自己立刻看到新值
强一致，所有读都反映最新写入
因果一致，只保证有依赖的顺序
options_en: Eventual consistency, which may take a while to converge.
Read-your-own-writes, where only you see your new value immediately.
Strong consistency, where every read reflects the latest write.
Causal consistency, which only preserves order for dependent events.
why: 账户余额要求绝对准确，任何读都要反映最新写，这就是强一致——性能代价最高但金融系统必需。
why_en: Bank balances require strong consistency so every read reflects the most recent write.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是展示「大致余额/上次同步值」，可放宽到读己之写或最终一致以换性能；但可动用的真实余额不行。
tradeoff: 强一致（准确但更慢） vs 更弱一致性模型（更快但可能旧）
codeSample:
table.get_item(
    Key={"acctId": "123"},
    ConsistentRead=True
)
# True  -> strong read, always latest write (higher latency)
# False -> eventually consistent read (default, cheaper, may lag)
optionExplanations: 银行必须强一致。
读己之写不足以保证账户余额准确。
正确，账户余额必须强一致。
因果一致不足以保证金融准确性。
optionExplanations_en: Banks require strong consistency, not eventual.
Read-your-own-writes is insufficient for account balance accuracy.
Correct, account balances require strong consistency to be accurate.
Causal consistency is insufficient for critical financial data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有读都反映最近一次写入。

termDefinitions.meaning: 变更数据捕获：捕捉主库的数据变更并异步推给副本、缓存等下游系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change Data Capture tracks changes in the primary database and propagates them asynchronously to replicas and caches.

scenario: 选型评审上有人说「DynamoDB 是 AP 数据库，我们这条订座路径要强一致，所以必须整体换成 PostgreSQL」。
scenario_en: In a design review someone says "DynamoDB is an AP database, and our seat-booking path needs strong consistency, so we must swap the whole thing for PostgreSQL".
q: 给数据库贴 CP/AP 标签这件事，正确的说法是？
q_en: What is the correct view of labelling a database as CP or AP?
options: CP/AP 是产品出厂就固定的属性，DynamoDB 在任何配置下都只能返回最终一致的读
多数现代分布式数据库可配置，同一技术既能强一致也能高可用
只要选了 Cassandra 这类系统，就无法在任何单个操作上拿到更强的一致性保证
一致性级别只是运维旋钮，跟应用正确性无关，设计阶段不必拿出来讨论
options_en: CP or AP is a fixed product property, and DynamoDB returns only eventually consistent reads in any configuration.
Most modern distributed databases are configurable — one technology can serve both strong consistency and high availability.
Once you pick something like Cassandra you can never get a stronger consistency guarantee on any single operation.
Consistency level is just an ops knob unrelated to application correctness, so it need not be discussed at design time.
why: 文章把 DynamoDB 同时列进「优先一致性」和「优先可用性」两张清单——差别在配置（强一致读模式 vs 多可用区）。代价是你要在每条访问路径上显式选一次，不能用一句「我们用 X」带过。
why_en: DynamoDB appears on both the consistency-first and availability-first lists because the difference is configuration, so you must choose explicitly per access path rather than hiding behind the product name.
optionExplanations: DynamoDB 有强一致读模式，正是文章列在「优先一致性」那一侧的技术之一。
正确：选型标签是二元的，实际系统不是——配置决定它站在 C 侧还是 A 侧。
把默认行为当成了唯一行为；默认最终一致不等于没有更强的选项。
读到旧值会不会超卖，是业务正确性问题，必须在非功能需求阶段就定。
optionExplanations_en: DynamoDB has a strongly consistent read mode and is listed among the consistency-first technologies.
Correct: the labels are binary but real systems are not — configuration decides which side it lands on.
This mistakes default behavior for the only behavior; an eventually consistent default is not the only option.
Whether a stale read causes overselling is business correctness and must be settled during non-functional requirements.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统在一致性、可用性、分区容错三者中最多同时满足两个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管键值/文档数据库，读取可选最终一致或强一致模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value and document database whose reads can be eventually or strongly consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向高可用与写扩展的分布式列式数据库，默认最终一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a distributed wide-column database built for high availability and write scaling, eventually consistent by default.

termDefinitions.meaning: AP 系统：分区发生时保住可用性，接受返回可能陈旧的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AP system keeps serving during a partition and accepts possibly stale data.

termDefinitions.meaning: CP 系统：分区发生时保住一致性，宁可拒绝请求也不返回旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CP system preserves consistency during a partition, rejecting requests rather than returning stale values.
